question: What's the best solar generator for power outages?
query: best solar generators portable power stations for home power outages 2026 reviews capacity expandable solar charging

replays.text:
**For serious home power outages, I’d pick the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has a 4,096Wh battery and 4,000W output, can expand up to 48kWh, and supports up to 2,600W of solar input—giving it more room to grow into a home-backup system than a typical portable station. It can also connect to an optional transfer-switch kit for essential home circuits. ([OutdoorGearLab’s testing](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

If you want something **lighter and easier to move**, consider the **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: it’s 39 lb, has a 2,042Wh capacity, and supports solar charging. It’s a better fit for selected essentials than for extended whole-home backup. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

One important caveat: solar power stations are quiet and produce no carbon monoxide, but they’re best suited to keeping a few essentials going—not necessarily powering a home for days. Solar recharging can be slow, especially in cloudy weather. ([Consumer Reports](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/))

**Bottom line:** DELTA Pro 3 for expandable home backup; Jackery 2000 v2 for a more portable setup. The right size depends on what you need to run—fridge, medical equipment, heating, or just phones and lights.

**Best for serious home outages: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has 4,096 Wh of capacity and 4,000 W of output, supports up to 2,600 W of solar input, and can expand to 48 kWh. It’s a strong choice if you want to run larger appliances or build a more substantial backup setup; an optional transfer-switch kit can connect it to essential home circuits. The trade-off is its size and likely higher cost. [OutdoorGearLab’s testing and review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**If portability matters more:** The **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** offers 2,042 Wh of capacity and weighs 39 lb, making it easier to move around. OutdoorGearLab says it can be paired with one or two 200 W solar panels. [See the review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

One important caveat: solar power stations are quiet and don’t produce carbon monoxide, but they’re usually better for keeping essentials going during shorter outages than powering a whole home for days. Solar recharging can also be slow, especially in cloudy weather. [Consumer Reports’ guide](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/)

**Best for serious home-outage backup: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has a **4,096Wh battery and 4,000W output**, supports expansion up to **48kWh**, and can take up to **2,600W of solar input**. It’s the strongest pick here if you want to run larger appliances or build toward backup for essential home circuits; EcoFlow offers an optional transfer-switch kit. ([OutdoorGearLab’s tested review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

If you want something easier to move, consider the **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: it weighs 39 lb, has 2,042Wh capacity, and supports solar charging. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

One caveat: even large power stations are usually best for **essential loads and shorter outages**, not running an entire home for days. Solar recharging can be slow, especially in cloudy weather.
